# PEN-3732 — pin the GitHub egress wrappers to the front of the agent Job's PATH

Applied as part of the PEN-3916 vendoring, in the same commit that brought this
tree in-tree. It is recorded as its own entry because it is the one place this
directory is **not** byte-for-byte upstream `133f4c1`.

`src/server/job-manifest.ts`, in `buildEnvVars()`: after the four env layers
collapse into `merged`, prepend `/usr/local/libexec/paperclip/bin` — the
root-owned directory the image installs the GitHub egress wrappers into — to
`merged.PATH`, idempotently, filtering any later duplicate. With no PATH to
prepend to it falls back to the system default rather than emitting a lone
directory, which would clobber the image's own `ENV PATH` (an explicit
container env entry wins outright) and leave nothing else resolvable.

`src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`: five cases under
`buildJobManifest — GitHub egress wrapper PATH ordering (PEN-3732)`.

## Why the adapter and not the chart

`paperclip.runtimePath` already fails the Helm render when a wrapper directory
is missing from PATH or lands after `/usr/bin`, but that guard only renders onto
the StatefulSet and the api Deployment. An agent Job's PATH comes from layer 3
(`selfPod.inheritedEnv`) or layer 4 (`adapterConfig.env.PATH`, an operator-set
database value), and layer 4 is a flat last-writer-wins assignment with no shape
check on any key. So the invariant was enforced everywhere except the containers
that actually run agents.

PEN-3713 fixed exactly this, in `buildEnvVars()` — but `buildEnvVars()` is owned
separately by each adapter, and that change reached `claude_k8s` only (PR #2185).
This is the mirror for `opencode_k8s`.

## Latent, not live — and why it was still worth carrying

There are no `opencode_k8s` workloads, so nothing was resolving `git` through
the agent-writable PVC wrappers in production. PEN-3732 measured the live PATH
on a pod labelled `paperclip.io/adapter-type=claude_k8s`, not an opencode one;
the gap here is structural rather than observed. Carrying it anyway, because the
cost of a latent gap in a security control is that it goes live silently the
first time an opencode Job is scheduled.

## Read the five test cases together

Each kills a mutant the others survive. Drop the operator case and an
implementation that only fixes the inherited path passes; drop the idempotence
case and one that prepends without de-duplicating passes, growing PATH on every
build; drop the no-PATH case and one that emits a lone directory passes; drop
the present-but-late case and one that checks only for PRESENCE passes — which
is the whole bug, since a PVC directory ahead of the wrappers resolves `git` to
the writable copy whether or not the wrapper directory appears later.

Verified by mutation at the time the patch was written, not assumed: with the
prepend removed, four of the five fail; with the guard and the de-dup filter
removed, the idempotence and present-but-late cases fail.

## Provenance of the patch itself

The patch text was authored on PR
[#2392](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/2392) and parked at
`vendor/opencode-k8s-patches/pen-3732-github-wrapper-path.patch` precisely
because there was nowhere to send it — no agent seat can push to
`kkroo/paperclip-adapter-opencode-k8s`. That PR never merged, so the patches
directory never existed on `master`; the content was carried directly into this
tree instead. #2392 is superseded by PEN-3916 and should be closed rather than
merged. Applied here with `patch -p1` against the `133f4c1` snapshot, clean, no
fuzz.

`GITHUB_WRAPPER_BIN_DIR` must stay equal to `paperclip.imageWrapperBinDir` in
the chart and to the identical constant in the `claude_k8s` adapter — three
places naming one directory. `deploy/helm/paperclip/tests/agent-egress-path.test.mjs`
asserts all of them.
